content: This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Cefotetan is an antibiotic used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It may also be administered before and during certain surgical procedures to help prevent infections. This medication belongs to the class of cephalosporin antibiotics. It is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections, such as the common cold or flu. Before using this medication, carefully read and follow all preparation and usage instructions provided by the manufacturer. Ensure proper mixing with the correct IV fluids as directed. Consult your pharmacist for additional details. Inspect the product visually for particles or discoloration before use. If you are using a frozen pre-mixed solution, thaw the container at room temperature or in the refrigerator. If thawed in the refrigerator, allow it to sit at room temperature for at least one hour before use. Do not thaw the solution using a water bath or microwave. After thawing, shake the container well and check for leaks by squeezing it. Discard the solution if the container leaks. For optimal effectiveness, administer this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. To help you remember, use it at the same time(s) every day. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed treatment period, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Learn how to store and safely discard needles and medical supplies. Common side effects may include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Rarely, this medication may cause loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headache. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. In rare cases, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using cefotetan, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Avoid consuming alcoholic beverages while taking this medication and for at least three days after completing it. Cefotetan may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefotetan may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine glucose tests or serum/urine creatinine tests, potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as complete blood count and kidney function tests, may be performed while you are using this product. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and use your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Different brands or packaging of this medication may have different storage requirements. Check the product package for instructions on how to store your brand, or ask your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete and personalized medical advice.
